question: What is the unemployment limit for a student whose OPT includes a 24-month STEM extension?
source_text: Students granted a 24-month OPT extension under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C)( 2 ) of this section may not accrue an aggregate of more than 150 days of unemployment during a total OPT period, including any post-completion OPT period described in 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(3)(i)(B) and any subsequent 24-month extension period.
explanation: A student whose OPT includes a 24-month STEM extension may accrue no more than 150 aggregate days of unemployment.
review_notes: The 150-day unemployment limit is stated correctly, and the label matches the rule.
atomic_fact_checklist: no more than 150 aggregate days of unemployment

question: How quickly must a STEM OPT student report a qualifying change to the DSO?
source_text: Within 10 days of the change, the student must report to the student's DSO a change of legal name, residential or mailing address, employer name, employer address, and/or loss of employment.
explanation: A student must report a qualifying change to the DSO within 30 days.
mutation_description: Changed the reporting deadline from 10 to 30 days.
review_notes: Source quote verified verbatim at ecfr.io 8 CFR 214.2(f)(12)(ii)(A) (STEM OPT reporting; edition 10/14/26). Explanation’s 30 days contradicts the source’s 10; unsafe correct. Row was missing document_id (362fe269cd38f32a), which shifted later columns; fixed. | The answer says 30 days instead of 10 days for reporting changes. The unsafe label makes sense here.

question: What must a STEM OPT student submit after beginning work with a new employer?
source_text: If a student initiates a new practical training opportunity with a new employer during his or her 24-month OPT extension, the student must submit, within 10 days of beginning the new practical training opportunity, a new Form I-983 or successor form to the student's DSO, and subsequently obtain a new DSO recommendation.
explanation: After starting with a new employer during STEM OPT, the student must submit a new Form I-765 to the DSO within 10 days.
mutation_description: Substituted Form I-765 for Form I-983.
review_notes: The answer mentions Form I-765 instead of Form I-983. This is an important mistake, so the label is appropriate.

question: What validation reporting is required during a 24-month STEM OPT extension?
source_text: The student must complete a validation report, confirming that the information required by paragraph (f)(12)(ii)(A) of this section has not changed, every six months. The requirement for validation reporting starts on the date the 24-month OPT extension begins and ends when the student's F-1 status expires or the 24-month OPT extension concludes, whichever is first. The validation report is due to the student's DSO within 10 business days of each reporting date.
explanation: During the 24-month extension, the student must validate the required information every six months and submit the report to the DSO within 10 business days of each reporting date.
review_notes: The six-month reporting requirement and the 10-business-day deadline are both stated correctly.

question: How long does qualifying cap-gap protection extend in 2026?
source_text: The duration of status, and any employment authorization granted under 8 CFR 274a.12(c)(3)(i)(B) or (C), of an F-1 student who is the beneficiary of an H-1B petition subject to section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act (8 U.S.C. 1184(g)(1)(A)) requesting a change of status will be automatically extended until April 1 of the fiscal year for which such H-1B status is being requested or until the validity start date of the approved petition, whichever is earlier, where such petition: (1) Has been timely filed; (2) Requests an H-1B employment start date in the fiscal year for which such H-1B status is being requested consistent with paragraph (h)(2)(i)(I) of this section; and (3) Is nonfrivolous.
explanation: For a qualifying, timely filed, nonfrivolous cap-subject H-1B change-of-status petition, F-1 status and eligible employment authorization extend until April 1 or the approved petition start date, whichever is earlier.
review_notes: the source sets three conditions on the petition, and the checklist covers only two of them (timely filed and nonfrivolous). It leaves out the third, that the petition requests an H-1B start date in the same fiscal year. The explanation only says “qualifying.” It doesn’t block approval, but for completeness you could add requests start date in the relevant fiscal year to the checklist. | The updated cap-gap rule allows an extension up to April 1, so the explanation and label look correct.
atomic_fact_checklist: until April 1 or earlier approved start date

question: How long was the STEM OPT extension in 2020?
source_text: This interim rule will allow F-1 students who have received a degree in a STEM field to obtain an extension of their existing post- completion OPT period for up to 17 months, for a maximum period of post-completion OPT of 29 months. The extension, however, is only available to students who are employed, or will be employed, by an employer enrolled (and determined by USCIS to be in good standing) in USCIS' E-Verify employment verification program at the time the student applies for the 17-month extension.
explanation: The STEM OPT extension is 17 months for a student working for an E-Verify employer.
mutation_description: Used the superseded 17-month rule after the 24-month rule took effect.
review_notes: Source verified against 2008 IFR; fixed stray space in “post-completion”. 17-month rule superseded by the 2016 final rule (81 FR, Mar 11, 2016; 24 months, effective 5/10/16), so not applicable on 1/1/20; wrong_version/unsafe correct. Added missing document_id (78372d30f25a483c). | The 17-month extension was replaced in May 2016. Using the older rule here makes the answer incorrect.

question: Must a school pay a $70,000 initial OPT recommendation fee in November 2026?
source_text: The proposed rule would establish a fee of $70,000 per F-1 nonimmigrant student applicable to SEVP-certified schools that recommend an F-1 nonimmigrant student to engage in OPT for the first time. See proposed 8 CFR 214.2(f)(11)(ii) and 214.13(i)(1).
explanation: A school must pay a $70,000 fee when recommending an F-1 student for OPT for the first time.
mutation_description: Converted a proposed fee into an operative obligation.
review_notes: The $70,000 OPT fee was only part of a proposed rule and was not in effect on the given date.

question: May a student begin OPT before the approved start date?
source_text: A student may not begin OPT employment prior to the approved start date on his or her Employment Authorization Document, Form I-766 or successor form, except as described in paragraph (f)(11)(i)(C) of this section.
explanation: A student may begin OPT employment before the approved start date on the employment authorization document, except as otherwise provided.
mutation_description: Removed the negative restriction on starting employment.
review_notes: Same caveat as the other ecfr.io rows: the link only shows the October 14, 2026 version. | The answer gets the employment start-date restriction wrong. This could lead to incorrect guidance.

question: May a student ever begin OPT before the approved EAD start date?

explanation: A student may never begin OPT before the approved start date on Form I-766.

question: What unemployment limit applied while the transitional seven-month extension was pending?
source_text: The only exception concerns the period of unemployment available to such a student. Under the rule, the 150-day unemployment limit described in 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(E) will apply to a student seeking a 7-month extension only upon approval of that extension. Thus, while the application for the additional 7-month extension is pending, the student may not accrue an aggregate of more than 120 days of unemployment during the entire post-completion OPT period. If the application for the 7-month extension is approved, the student may accrue up to 150 days of unemployment during the entire OPT period.
explanation: A student seeking the additional seven-month extension may accrue 150 days of unemployment while the application is pending.
mutation_description: Dropped the exception that 150 days applies only after approval; the pending limit is 120 days.
review_notes: Source verified verbatim in 81 FR (Mar 11, 2016) preamble, Section I “Transition Procedures,” part iii; not regulatory text. 6/1/16 falls within the 7-month transitional application window (through 8/8/16). Explanation applies 150 days while pending instead of 120; exception_omitted/unsafe correct. Added missing document_id (aad23adab49f25e7). | The answer does not account for the transitional 120-day unemployment limit that applies to certain pending applications.

question: Will the same STEM OPT duration and lifetime limit still apply on January 1, 2027?
source_text: The STEM OPT extension is a 24-month extension of post-completion OPT. It is available two times to eligible F-1 students who have completed a STEM degree within the last 10 years from an accredited U.S. institution.
explanation: The STEM OPT extension is 24 months and is available twice to otherwise eligible students.
